title: Fighting a racist in a bar with Billie and her ashtray
summary: After a man refused to speak to 'Niggers', Simmons and Billie beat him and six sailors outside.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: And then on another occassion, when Billie and I had a bout with some [sailors] We had been - - went to Vesuvius Res-
taurant. It's an Italian Restaurant on around about 44th Street.
Yeah, I think it was [Frascedelli's] (inaudible). Favorite Note.

MR. SIMMONS: It was close to Sixth Avenue. And all of a sudden it started raining, so we ran across the street to the bar and I stayed there. That's Billie's hangout, the bar. I get outside and I whistle for a cab and a cab would stop and before I could open the door some white man would open the door on the other side and jump in. Naturally the cab driver would take him.

So I called one back to the phone booth and called up Billie's job and had her to get the doorman to get a cab and come down there and pick us up. That's the only way we'd get up there because they was just taking cabs away from us, you know.

So while I'm making the phone call, she had this little wire-haired terrier named Moochie that someone had just given her the night before. And she had Moochie under her fur coat and this white couple was over in the corner with their backs turned to the streets, you know, facing the bar. Lady and I were in the midst of the bar, facing the bar and they were on the end with their backs turned to the bar. If you can visualize this. And the woman and Billie had a conversation going about dogs. And I got there just in time to see "Well
where I come from, we don't speak to Niggers." I say what did you say? "I said, sir, where we come from we don't speak to Niggers.

The fellow that was with the woman that was having the discussion with the dogs. He was her escort. So he says and if you would oblige me, you will step outside. I say yeah, right now, and I rushed around there and grabbed him by the coat collar. He wasn't anxious to go then. (Laughter).

So I started pulling on him and I'm pulling on him and Billie's behind him pushing him (Laughter). So we get to the door, he puts his foot behind the door to hang out to keep from going out. And she hit him in back of the head with one of these big thick diamond shaped ash trays. And that made him weakened a little bit and I snatched him out there on the side walk out there in the rain. And I beat a tattoo on that side-walk with his head.

And all of a sudden here come about six of his majesty's seamen. Running to his help. So I stepped back in the door way. And as fast as they stepped up, I would pop one and Billie stepped outside the door to keep from getting wet in the rain. And as fast as he would walk up, I would pop one, the next one that come up was hers. (Laughter). She would hit him in the face with the ashtray. (Laughter). So we had seven bodies laying out there in front of the bar. Finally a cab

showed up. We had done a night's work already.
So we got back. I went to my job. I was sitting in
the dressing room trying to dry off. Try to get myself present-
able for the bandstand. But her gowns was in her dressing room,
so she didn't have any problem changing, you know.
